body.p: Claims 1-20 will be pending after entry of the present paper. Claims 1-8, 10-16, and 18- 20 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally filed specification, drawings, and claims. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the amendments and remarks submitted herein.

The Office Action rejects claims 1-5, 9-11, 14-16 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0164988 to Alvarez ("Alvarez"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

"[T]he hallmark of anticipation is prior invention" and "the prior art reference - in order to anticipate under 35 U.S.C. § 102 - must not only disclose all elements of the claim within the four comers of the document, but must also disclose those elements arranged as in the claim." NetMoneyln, Inc. v. VeriSign, Inc., 545 F.3d 1359, 1369 (Fed. Cir. 2008). Applicant respectfully submits that the claims as amended are not anticipated.
Claim 1 is amended to recite:
A system for touchless control of a lavatory of an aircraft, the system
comprising:
a plurality of touchless sensors located in the lavatory, wherein each of
the plurality of touchless sensors is configured to receive data corresponding to
the lavatory;
an actuator located in the lavatory and configured to perform a first
action;
a light source located in the lavatory and configured to perform a second
action; and
a central controller coupled to the plurality of touchless sensors, the
actuator, and the light source, the central controller configured to make an
inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received
from each of the plurality of touchless sensors and to control at least one of the
actuator and the light source based on the inference.

Alvarez fails to contemplate or disclose each and every element of claim 1 as amended herein. Specifically, Alvarez fails to contemplate or disclose at least "the central controller configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors." The Office Action asserts that the claimed "configured to make an inference" is "shown in logic diagram in figure 2" of Alvarez. (Office

Action, page 3.) With respect to FIG. 2, Alvarez describes "a flow chart of an occupancy detection method for a lavatory" including receiving "a door sensor signal from the door sensor 116." (Alvarez, [0050].) However, Alvarez does not contemplate or disclose at least "make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors" as recited by claim 1. Therefore, Alvarez does not contemplate or disclose each and every element of amended claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 10 is amended similar to claim 1 and is therefore patentable over Alvarez for at least the same reasons discussed above. Claims 2-5, 9, 11, 14-16, and 20 depend from claims 1 and 10, respectively, and are patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above, further in view of their own respective features. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-5, 9-11, 14-16, and 20 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

The Office Action rejects claims 6, 7, 12, 17 and 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Alvarez in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2018/0369434 to Callahan ("Callahan"). The Office Action rejects claims 8, 13 and 19 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Alvarez in view of Callahan with respect to the health status of a system using UV lights as applied to claims 6, 12 and 17 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2008/0131332 ("Nguyen"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

The cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose or contemplate each and every element of the claims as amended herein. Claims 6-8, 12, 13, and 17-19 depend from claims 1 and 10, respectively, and are therefore patentable over the cited references for at least the same reasons as described above, further in view of their own respective features. As discussed above, Alvarez fails to teach or disclose at least "the central controller configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors" and the other references fail to cure that deficiency. Specifically, Callahan describes "a method of operating a UV light source for a vehicle includes measuring an amount of power on a commodity power feeder." (Callahan, Abstract.) Nguyen describes "[a] disinfectant dispensing system includes a dispensing device implemented to dispense a predetermined amount of disinfectant." (Nguyen, Abstract.) Neither reference, either

alone or in combination with Alvarez, discloses or contemplates "the central controller configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors" as recited by claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 6-8, 12, 13, and 17-19 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks and amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if doing so will further prosecution of the subject application. The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees that may be required or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 192814. This statement does NOT authorize charge of the issue fee.
Respectfully submitted,
